mainTopic: Food that is temporarily unfit on שבת or יום טוב, and whether a בכור's blemish may be examined on יום טוב
overview: This amud opens at the end of a proof. Bubbling pots of food are not yet edible, but they become fit to eat once they finish cooking. אביי rejects the proof, because ordinary Shabbos pots work the same way and nobody questions them. So the question is narrowed to food that nature finishes (בידי שמים), and that question stays unresolved. Next, רבי יהודה נשיאה sends a בכור to רבי אמי and then to רבי יצחק נפחא. Each time they hesitate to examine it, a student reminds them that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון. רבי אבא challenges this with a report that רבי זירא ruled like רבי שמעון. רבי זירא himself later clarifies that he only said 'it stands to reason.' רב יוסף then cites an old ירושלים tradition, read as following רבי מאיר's view that a בכור must be examined while alive and so before יום טוב. אביי rejects that proof, showing that רבי מאיר's ruling is only a penalty, and רב נחמן בר יצחק supports him from the משנה's wording. The amud ends with a story: רבי אמי approved of an examiner who would not check בכורות on יום טוב, and he himself checked only on the day before.

steps.title: Finished cooking makes the food fit again
steps.stepSummary: The proof ends: once the cooking is finished, the food becomes fit to eat again.
steps.simpleTranslation: When their cooking is finished, they are fit for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a proof from the previous lines. Bubbling pots of food are not edible while they boil, yet once the cooking is done they become fit again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the proof is that food can be unfit for part of the day and still become permitted later. So something pushed aside for a while (נדחה) does not have to stay forbidden all day. This would answer the question of whether there is מוקצה for half a day.

keyTerms.meaning: they are fit (for use or eating)
something set aside and not usable on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: When their cooking is finished, they are fit.
phrases.notes: "They" means the pots of food from the proof just before, which were not yet edible while still bubbling.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר בִּשּׁוּלַיְיהוּ חֲזוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that started before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That food can be temporarily unfit and still become permitted later in the same day (no permanent דיחוי).
steps.raayaSupportSource: Pots of food that are bubbling and inedible, then become edible once cooked.

steps.title: אביי: every ordinary pot would be a problem
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the proof cannot be right, because ordinary Shabbos pots work the same way and everyone eats from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: According to your reasoning, ordinary pots should be a problem for you. Ordinary pots are usually still boiling at twilight, and in the evening we eat from them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. Using that logic, every regular pot on Shabbos would also be a problem, and that cannot be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food that is still boiling at בין השמשות is not edible at the moment Shabbos starts. Yet everyone eats it Friday night, and nobody thinks this is a question. So this kind of case cannot be what the original question was about, and the proof proves nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: it should be difficult for you

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And according to your reasoning, ordinary pots should be difficult for you,
for ordinary pots, in general,
are boiling at twilight,
and in the evening we eat from them!
phrases.notes: He means Friday night, after Shabbos has already started.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וּלְטַעְמָיךְ תִּקְשֵׁי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 1.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is no different from ordinary Shabbos pots, which nobody questions, so it cannot settle the real question.

steps.title: The question is only about food finished by nature
steps.stepSummary: In response to אביי, the question is narrowed. Food that people finish was never in doubt. The doubt is only about food that is finished by nature.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we have no question about something whose completion is done by a person. Our question is about something whose completion is done by Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: After אביי's objection, the גמרא redefines what the question really is. It only applies to food that becomes ready by itself, such as fruit drying in the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person controls the process, as with cooking, the food is clearly expected to be ready and is never pushed aside. When nature controls it, as with figs or grapes drying, it is less clear, and that is the open question. The proof from pots does not touch this case, so the question stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: its completion is done by a person
its completion is done by Heaven, meaning by nature
we have no question about it

steps.whatToRemember: Food that a person finishes, like a cooking pot, can always be eaten once it is ready. The open question (מוקצה לחצי שבת) is only about food that nature finishes, and it is not answered here.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the question was solved. It is saying the proof missed the point, because it dealt with the case nobody was asking about.

phrases.english: Rather, its completion by a person
we have no question about.
When we do have a question,
it is about its completion by Heaven.
phrases.notes: "By Heaven" means it gets ready on its own, without a person doing anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּמָרוֹ בִּידֵי אָדָם לָא קָא מִבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's rejection by redefining the scope of the original question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of מוקצה for part of the day applies only to things finished by nature. Things finished by a person are clearly permitted once ready.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה sends a בכור to רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: A story begins. רבי יהודה נשיאה had a בכור and sent it to רבי אמי to be examined, but רבי אמי leaned toward not examining it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה had a certain firstborn animal. He sent it before רבי אמי, who thought he should not examine it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of examining a בכור on יום טוב and tells a story. This step sets up the scene for the correction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור can only be eaten after an expert confirms it has a blemish. רבי אמי's hesitation fits the view of רבי שמעון, who is stricter here. The story leads into which opinion we actually follow.

keyTerms.meaning: to examine it, to look at it

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא בּוּכְרָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia had a certain firstborn animal.
He sent it before Rabbi Ami,
phrases.notes: He sent it so רבי אמי could check whether its blemish permits it to be eaten.

phrases.english: who thought not to examine it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא בּוּכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, returning to the earlier discussion of a בכור on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי was inclined not to examine the בכור on יום טוב.

steps.title: The rule is like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא (or רבי ירמיה) reminds רבי אמי that when רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא, and some say רבי ירמיה, said to him: Between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A student corrects רבי אמי by quoting a general rule for deciding the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows examining the בכור, and רבי שמעון does not. By the standard rule, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so the animal should be examined.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (another name for the speaker)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the general rule this student relies on. The next steps challenge it with a report that רבי זירא leaned toward רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זְרִיקָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika, and some say Rabbi Yirmeya, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon: the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects רבי אמי's hesitation from step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אמי's inclination not to examine the בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It follows רבי שמעון, but the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The בכור is sent to רבי יצחק נפחא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה then sent the בכור to רבי יצחק נפחא, who also leaned toward not examining it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then sent it before רבי יצחק נפחא, who also thought not to examine it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story repeats with a second חכם, who has the same hesitation. This sets up a second, matching correction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two leading חכמים both leaned toward the stricter view of רבי שמעון. This shows that the hesitation was a real position, which is why the rule had to be stated again.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר שַׁדְּרֵיהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: He then sent it before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
who thought not to examine it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר שַׁדְּרֵיהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 4 with a second חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק נפחא also leaned toward not examining the בכור.

steps.title: Again: the rule is like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה (or רבי זריקא) gives the same reminder: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה, and some say רבי זריקא, said to him: Between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The same correction is given to the second חכם, with the two names of the speakers in reverse order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the rule a second time strengthens it: the בכור should be examined, following רבי יהודה. The names are swapped because the tradition is unsure which student said which line.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the students who gave the correction
the other student named as the possible speaker

steps.whatToRemember: Twice, a great חכם leaned toward רבי שמעון's strict view. Twice he was reminded of the general rule that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון. The next steps challenge this reminder.
steps.confusionAlert: Look closely at the names. In step 5 the main speaker is רבי זריקא, with "some say רבי ירמיה." Here it is reversed. It is the same rule, not a new opinion.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי זְרִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya, and some say Rabbi Zerika, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon: the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי זְרִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects רבי יצחק נפחא, matching step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יצחק נפחא's inclination not to examine the בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It follows רבי שמעון, but the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why did you stop the רבנן from following רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges רבי ירמיה for not letting the חכמים act like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: Why didn't you let the רבנן act in practice like רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא pushes back on the reminder from the last step that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two great רבנן had leaned toward not checking the בכור, which is רבי שמעון's view. רבי ירמיה stopped them. Now רבי אבא asks what right he had to stop them, which suggests רבי אבא thinks רבי שמעון's view is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: You let them, you allowed them
To act in practice, to make an actual ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי ירמיה, who gave the reminder in the previous step.

phrases.english: What is the reason you did not let the Sages
act in practice according to Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי טעמא לא שבקתינהו לרבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reminder given in steps 5 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's stopping the חכמים from following רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is reason to follow רבי שמעון, then stopping great רבנן from acting on his view was wrong.

steps.title: What source do you have?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי אבא what source he has for following רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And you, what do you have in your hand?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge with a question. He asks what source backs רבי שמעון. This sets up רבי אבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule from step 5 favors רבי יהודה. So whoever wants to follow רבי שמעון needs a specific tradition, and רבי ירמיה asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What do you have in your hand? (What source do you have?)

phrases.english: He said to him: And you, what do you have in your hand?
phrases.notes: He means: do you have a tradition that says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?

steps.triggerLanguage: ואת מה בידך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אבא's challenge by asking for his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What tradition supports ruling like רבי שמעון?

steps.title: רבי זירא said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that רבי זירא ruled the הלכה is like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי זירא said: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives his source: a ruling he heard in the name of רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A specific ruling about this case would override the general rule that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון. That is why רבי אבא felt the חכמים should have been allowed to act.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Zeira said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכי אמר רבי זירא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי זירא ruled הלכה כרבי שמעון.

steps.title: Someone wants to hear it from רבי זירא himself
steps.stepSummary: An unnamed person hopes to go to ארץ ישראל and learn the ruling directly from רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain person said: May I merit to go up there and learn this teaching from the mouth of its master.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. Someone wants to check the report by asking רבי זירא in person. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling reached him secondhand, through רבי אבא. Hearing it from the source himself would confirm exactly what was said.

keyTerms.meaning: I will go up there (to ארץ ישראל)
From the mouth of its master

phrases.english: A certain person said:
May I merit to go up there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל, where רבי זירא was.

phrases.english: and learn the teaching
from the mouth of its master.
phrases.notes: The 'master' of this teaching is רבי זירא himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר מאן דהוא אזכי ואסק להתם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets out to check the report given in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling attributed to רבי זירא should be checked directly with him.

steps.title: רבי זירא: I only said it is reasonable
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא denies saying a firm 'הלכה כרבי שמעון'. He only said 'מסתברא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he went up there, he found רבי זירא and asked: Did the master say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון? He said: No. I said, 'It stands to reason.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא corrects the report. He never gave a firm ruling. He only said רבי שמעון's view seems reasonable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a real difference between 'the הלכה is so' and 'it stands to reason.' The first is a firm ruling. The second is only a reasoned leaning. So רבי אבא's source is weaker than he presented it.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it seems logical

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying רבי שמעון is wrong. He is only saying his words were a reasoned opinion, not a firm ruling of הלכה.

phrases.english: When he went up there,
he found Rabbi Zeira and said to him:
Did the master say the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon?
He said to him: No,
I said, 'It stands to reason.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה לא אנא מסתברא אמרי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the wording of the ruling reported in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי זירא gave a firm ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אבא reported a 'מסתברא' as if it were a firm 'הלכה'.

steps.title: Why רבי זירא thought רבי שמעון's view is reasonable
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains: the משנה gives this view in רבי שמעון's name, and a ברייתא gives it in the name of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches: רבי שמעון says, any animal whose blemish was not noticeable while it was still day is not among the prepared; and a ברייתא teaches the same in the name of the חכמים. Learn from this that it stands to reason to follow him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the basis for his 'מסתברא'. The same view shows up in a ברייתא as the opinion of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, this view belongs to one person, רבי שמעון. The ברייתא presents it as the view of the חכמים, which shows it had wider support. That makes it reasonable to lean toward it, even without a firm tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: While it was still day, before יום טוב began
Prepared, set aside before יום טוב for use on יום טוב
In the name of the Sages, as a group view

phrases.english: Since it teaches in our Mishnah:
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִיכָּר מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
phrases.english: any animal whose blemish was not noticeable while it was still day
is not among the prepared,
and a Baraita teaches it in the name of the Sages,
learn from this that it stands to reason to follow him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מדקתני במתניתין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis for the 'מסתברא' of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That it is reasonable to follow רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that presents רבי שמעון's view as the view of the חכמים
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's position is only a reasoned leaning toward רבי שמעון. It rests on the ברייתא presenting this view as the view of the חכמים.

steps.title: So what is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final conclusion is on this matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What came of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The story left things unclear, so the גמרא asks for the bottom line. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule favors רבי יהודה, but רבי זירא leaned toward רבי שמעון. The גמרא wants a clear ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What came of it? What is the conclusion?

phrases.english: What came of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי הוי עלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a final ruling after the unresolved story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view is the final הלכה?

steps.title: An old tradition from ירושלים: the הלכה is like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites a long chain of tradition going back to the holy community of ירושלים: הלכה כרבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear, for this hangs on great trees. רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול, in the name of רבי, in the name of the holy community in ירושלים: רבי שמעון and his colleagues said the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers with a ruling handed down through a chain of great sages: the הלכה is like רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Hangs on great trees' means this question depends on a disagreement among great early sages. רב יוסף cites a tradition passed through several links back to the holy community in ירושלים. It reports that רבי שמעון and his colleagues held like רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Great trees (a picture for great sages)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'רבי שמעון' in this chain is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. He is not the רבי שמעון of our משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear,
for it hangs on great trees.
phrases.notes: A picture: this question goes back to a disagreement among great early sages.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: that Rebbi said in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon and his colleagues said
the halacha follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יוסף תא שמע דתליא באשלי רברבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with an old tradition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The holy community of ירושלים ruled הלכה כרבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It brings an early, highly respected tradition into the discussion. The next steps reread its wording, and then אביי challenges the proof built on it.

steps.title: How could older sages rule like a younger one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב יוסף's tradition. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא and his colleagues were much older than רבי מאיר, so how could they have 'said' the הלכה follows him?
steps.simpleTranslation: They 'said' it? But they are much older than him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks on one word in the tradition from step 15, 'they said'. It points out that the sages who supposedly said it were much older than רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a younger sage might say 'the הלכה follows' an older or earlier sage. It sounds strange for much older sages to announce that the הלכה follows a younger one. So the wording of the tradition needs to be explained.

phrases.english: They said?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the tradition from step 15, where רבי שמעון בן מנסיא and his colleagues 'said' the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: But they are much older than him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִינְהוּ קַשִּׁישֵׁי מִנֵּיהּ טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the tradition cited in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'they said הלכה כרבי מאיר' in רב יוסף's tradition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sages much older than רבי מאיר would not phrase their ruling as 'the הלכה follows' him.

steps.title: They ruled according to רבי מאיר's approach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the tradition. The older sages did not 'rule like' רבי מאיר. Their position simply matches רבי מאיר's line of thinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: they said it according to the approach of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The older sages held a view that follows the same reasoning as רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no problem of older sages deferring to a younger one. Their ruling that blemishes may not be examined on יום טוב simply fits רבי מאיר's way of thinking. This sets up the next step, which shows where רבי מאיר's approach is found.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the approach or reasoning of

phrases.english: Rather:
They said it according to the approach of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by rereading the tradition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the tradition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The older sages declared that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The older sages held a view built on רבי מאיר's reasoning.

steps.title: The משנה of the בכור slaughtered before being shown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source for רבי מאיר's approach. A בכור was slaughtered before an expert checked its blemish. רבי יהודה permits it and רבי מאיר forbids it. This seems to show that רבי מאיר holds a בכור must be examined while alive, unlike a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If one slaughtered a בכור and only afterward showed its blemish to an expert, רבי יהודה permits it. רבי מאיר says: since it was slaughtered without an expert's approval, it is forbidden. So רבי מאיר holds that examining a בכור is not like examining a טרפה. A בכור is examined while alive, and a טרפה after slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to show where 'רבי מאיר's approach' comes from. It then draws out what רבי מאיר must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be slaughtered outside the בית המקדש if it has a permanent blemish confirmed by an expert. רבי מאיר forbids it even when the blemish is confirmed afterward. The גמרא reads this as meaning a בכור's examination is a formal ruling that must happen while the animal is alive. Checking a טרפה is different: it is just finding out the facts, which can be done after slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn kosher animal, which belongs to a כהן
An expert sage who rules on blemishes
An animal with a fatal defect, which is not kosher

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
One who slaughters the firstborn
and afterward showed its blemish to an expert —
Rabbi Yehuda permits it.
And Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Since it was slaughtered without an expert's approval, it is forbidden.
Apparently Rabbi Meir holds:
Examining a firstborn is not like examining a tereifa;
examining a firstborn is done while it is alive,
examining a tereifa is done after slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the source of 'רבי מאיר's approach' mentioned in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר treats examining a בכור as different from examining a טרפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a בכור slaughtered before its blemish was shown, where רבי מאיר forbids it.

steps.title: So a טרפה may be checked on יום טוב, but a בכור only before
steps.stepSummary: From רבי מאיר's distinction, the older sages concluded: a טרפה may be examined even on יום טוב, but a בכור must be examined on ערב יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from this: examining a טרפה may be done even on יום טוב, but examining a בכור must be done on ערב יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the line of reasoning. It shows how רבי מאיר's distinction leads to the older sages' rule about יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Examining a בכור counts as a formal ruling, more like judging, so it may not be done on יום טוב. Checking a טרפה is just finding out a fact, so it is allowed even on יום טוב. This explains how the older sages' view is 'according to רבי מאיר's approach'.

phrases.english: And from this:
examining a tereifa may be done even on a Festival,
examining a firstborn must be done from the eve of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical יום טוב rule from the distinction made in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this reading, a טרפה may be examined on יום טוב, but a בכור's blemish must be examined before יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי: that dispute is about a penalty
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר are not arguing about how blemishes are examined. They are arguing about whether to penalize someone who slaughtered too early.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do they really argue there about examining blemishes? They argue about a penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof from steps 18-19. He says the משנה has nothing to do with how or when a בכור's blemish may be examined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, רבי מאיר forbids the animal only to punish the person who slaughtered without waiting for an expert. If that is the reason, the משנה tells us nothing about examining blemishes on יום טוב. The whole proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Do you really think?
A penalty imposed by the rabbis

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say רבי מאיר allows the animal. He agrees רבי מאיר forbids it. He only changes the reason: it is a penalty, not a rule about how a בכור must be examined.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רב יוסף, who brought the tradition.

phrases.english: Is that to say that there they disagree about examining blemishes?
They disagree about a penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ הָתָם, בְּרוֹאִין מוּמִין פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה used in steps 18-19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי מאיר requires a בכור to be examined while alive, and the יום טוב rule drawn from it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute in the משנה is about penalizing improper slaughter, not about how blemishes are examined.

steps.title: Proof: blemishes in the eyelids
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his reading with רבי יוחנן's statement. If the blemish is in the eyelids, everyone agrees the animal is forbidden, because such blemishes change after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: with blemishes in the eyelids, everyone agrees it is forbidden, because they change.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source to back up his claim that the argument is about a penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eyelid blemishes can look different after the animal dies, so they cannot be judged properly after slaughter. That is why everyone forbids those. This implies that for ordinary blemishes, which do not change, the blemish can be checked after death, so רבי מאיר's prohibition must be only a penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: The eyelids, the skin around the eye

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר is limited to blemishes that can still be checked properly after death. That fits אביי's view that it is about a penalty.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
With blemishes in the eyelids —
everyone agrees that it is forbidden,
because they change.
phrases.notes: After the animal dies, an eyelid blemish can look different, so it can no longer be judged properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's rejection in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר is about a penalty, not about how blemishes are examined.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement (through רבה בר בר חנה) that everyone forbids the animal when the blemish is in the eyelids, because such blemishes change after death.

steps.title: The real disagreement is about body blemishes
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה actually disagree: blemishes on the body. רבי מאיר makes a גזירה because of eye blemishes, and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about blemishes on the body. רבי מאיר says we forbid those too, because people might confuse them with eye blemishes. רבי יהודה says we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's reading. Eye blemishes are forbidden by everyone, so the argument must be about body blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Body blemishes do not change after death, so in principle they can be checked after slaughtering. רבי מאיר still forbids them as a protective decree, so people won't do the same with eye blemishes, which do change. This means the argument is about a rabbinic fence, not about how blemishes are checked.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemishes on the body (like a cut ear or broken leg)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that רבי מאיר thinks body blemishes must be checked while the animal is alive. He forbids them only as a decree, so people won't confuse them with eye blemishes.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is with blemishes in the body,
Rabbi Meir holds:
We decree to forbid blemishes in the body
because of blemishes in the eye.
phrases.notes: Eye blemishes are the ones from Step 21 that change after death.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: we do not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּמוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's reading: since everyone forbids eye blemishes (Step 21), the argument is only about body blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids a בכור with a body blemish slaughtered without an expert, as a decree because of eye blemishes. רבי יהודה permits it.

steps.title: The משנה's wording shows it is a penalty
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points to רבי מאיר's words, 'since it was slaughtered without an expert.' This shows his ruling is a penalty. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the משנה's wording supports this. רבי מאיר says, 'Since it was slaughtered without an expert, it is forbidden.' So he is giving a penalty. Yes, that is the lesson.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings support for אביי from the exact words of the משנה. The גמרא agrees with the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not say 'because it can't be checked anymore.' He says 'because it was slaughtered without an expert,' which blames the person's action. That points to a קנס for acting too early, not to a rule about checking.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise, its exact wording supports this
An expert who decides on בכור blemishes

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי מאיר's ruling is a penalty for slaughtering without an expert. It is not a rule that a בכור can only be checked while alive. So the older sages' conclusion from Step 19 loses its proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the source for the idea that a בכור must be checked on ערב יום טוב. Even so, the story that follows shows רבי אמי approving the practice of not checking on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The Mishnah is also precise this way,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה in בכורות that we quoted in Step 18.

phrases.english: for it teaches: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Since it was slaughtered not by the word of an expert, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: קְנָסָא הוּא דְּקָא קָנֵיס,
phrases.english: Learn from this: it is a penalty that he is imposing.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the wording of the משנה to אביי's reading in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר's ruling is a penalty
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's words in the משנה: 'since it was slaughtered without an expert'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר's prohibition is a קנס, not a rule about how a בכור is checked.

steps.title: The examiner who did not check בכורות on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אמי ורדינאה checked בכורות for the נשיא's household but would not check them on יום טוב. רבי אמי said he was doing the right thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמי ורדינאה checked firstborn animals for the נשיא's household. On יום טוב he would not check them. People told רבי אמי, and he said: he is doing the right thing by not checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about checking a בכור's blemish on יום טוב. רבי אמי approves of not checking on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the proof was rejected, this story shows a real practice of not checking בכורות on יום טוב. It also sets up a question about רבי אמי's own behavior.

phrases.english: Ami of Vardina
was the examiner of firstborns for the house of the Nasi.
On Yom Tov he would not examine.
They came and told Rabbi Ami.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: שַׁפִּיר קָא עָבֵיד דְּלָא חָזֵי.
phrases.english: He said to them: he does well not to examine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּי וַרְדִּינָאָה חָזֵי בּוּכְרָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the analysis of רבי מאיר to a story about actual practice for checking a בכור on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי approved of not checking בכורות on יום טוב.

steps.title: But רבי אמי himself checked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can רבי אמי praise someone for not checking, when רבי אמי himself checked בכורות?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רבי אמי himself check בכורות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. רבי אמי's own behavior seems to contradict his praise of not checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It was known that רבי אמי checked בכורות, apparently on יום טוב. If he did, why would he approve of someone refusing to check?

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rabbi Ami himself examines!
phrases.notes: The question assumes רבי אמי checked on יום טוב itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי גּוּפֵיהּ חָזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's approval in Step 24 using his own practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's praise of not checking on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אמי himself checked בכורות, so he seems to permit it.

steps.title: רבי אמי checked the day before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אמי did not check on יום טוב. He checked the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אמי checked, he did it the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי אמי's checking was done on ערב יום טוב, not on יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there is no contradiction. רבי אמי checked before יום טוב, which fits his approval of not checking on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: From yesterday, on the day before

phrases.english: When Rabbi Ami would examine,
he would examine from the day before,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי כִּי חָזֵי מֵאֶתְמוֹל הֲוָה חָזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25 by changing when רבי אמי checked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי checked בכורות on יום טוב itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי checked on ערב יום טוב, so his practice fits his ruling.
